name: Traefik Ingress Health
description: Incoming application traffic, errors, response times, and certificate expiry.

display.name: How to read incoming traffic
display.description: HTTP at the proxy includes health checks, APIs, authentication, and other automated calls.

spec.text:
**Totals** cover the selected period. **Traffic and response time** use five-minute windows. Short benchmarks use a different window: allow ingestion, then click **Refresh**.

**Average:** 50, 100 and 150 ms average 100 ms. **p95:** about 95 of 100 calls finish within this time. Traefik measures server traffic; browser timing includes the network. Totals include automated calls and may be incomplete for new series or collection gaps. After changing Cluster, reset the other filters to Everything.

display.name: Requests/s · 5-minute average
display.description:
Requests averaged over five minutes. A brief load test is diluted by the quiet part of that window. Select its application before comparing traffic.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Operational context: no standalone alert; compare with the related error, latency, capacity or collection monitor

display.name: Average response time · 5 min · ms
display.description:
How long a request takes on average to get a response, measured by Traefik for the selected applications. Add all response times and divide by the number of completed requests. Example: calls taking 50, 100, and 150 ms give an average of 100 ms. Lower means faster responses. A few slow calls can be hidden by this average; also check the 95-of-100 response time. Browser timing includes extra network time. Without completed requests, this value is unavailable.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Traefik p95 response above 3s · 10m. The estimated 95th-percentile response time exceeds 3 seconds. This means the boundary below which about 95% of requests finish is above 3 seconds; it does not mean 95% of requests take longer than 3 seconds. Requires at least 100 requests per five-minute calculation window, persisting over observed samples for ten minutes. Replace this starting threshold with the service objective.

display.name: 95% of calls finish within · 5 min · ms
display.description:
If this shows 200 ms, about 95 out of 100 calls finished within 200 ms and the other five took longer. This is the p95 response time: it helps spot slow experiences that an average can hide. It is estimated from Traefik measurements for the selected applications over the last hour, including earlier tests. Lower means faster responses. Browser measurements can differ because they include extra network time. Uses the same five-minute window as average response time. The average can exceed p95 when a few requests take an exceptionally long time, such as long polling.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Traefik p95 response above 3s · 10m. The estimated 95th-percentile response time exceeds 3 seconds. This means the boundary below which about 95% of requests finish is above 3 seconds; it does not mean 95% of requests take longer than 3 seconds. Requires at least 100 requests per five-minute calculation window, persisting over observed samples for ten minutes. Replace this starting threshold with the service objective.

display.name: Response time · average, p50, p95, p99 · ms
display.description:
Each point summarizes the preceding five minutes. Average adds all response times and divides by completed requests. Half of calls (p50) finished within that line's time; 95 of 100 (p95) and 99 of 100 (p99) show how long slower calls took. Example: p95 of 200 ms means about 95% finished within 200 ms and 5% took longer. Rising lines mean slower responses. Traefik estimates these percentiles from timing buckets; without calls, no response time can be calculated.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Traefik p95 response above 3s · 10m. The estimated 95th-percentile response time exceeds 3 seconds. This means the boundary below which about 95% of requests finish is above 3 seconds; it does not mean 95% of requests take longer than 3 seconds. Requires at least 100 requests per five-minute calculation window, persisting over observed samples for ten minutes. Replace this starting threshold with the service objective.

display.name: HTTP 5xx · application and time
display.description:
Each line identifies the cluster, namespace, application and response code. Hover over a peak to see its time window. Each point estimates errors in the preceding chart interval, which grows when you zoom out. Adjacent windows can overlap: do not add the points to obtain a total. Scrapes are normally 30 seconds apart. Exact request timestamps and the reason require access logs and application logs/traces. A 5xx is a server-side failure; a 4xx is a rejected request, not necessarily an outage.

When to investigate / alert coverage: Traefik HTTP 5xx above 5 percent · 5m. More than 5% of completed requests fail with HTTP 5xx, with at least 100 requests in each observed five-minute calculation window. The condition must persist over observed samples for five minutes. Uses Traefik counters, not span sampling.
